TOP RECOMMENDATION: Replace the upstream P0D volume with a SuperFGD fully-active 3D scintillator cube detector (1 cm³ polystyrene cubes read on three faces by WLS fibres and MPPCs), which is the single change that enables 4π reconstruction of low-momentum recoil protons at all angles and is the irreplaceable foundation for all TKI measurements required to meet the T2K-II systematic uncertainty target.

# Hardware Upgrade Proposals for the Near Detector Active Target Module

## Context and Constraints Summary

The available envelope is **2.0 m × 1.9 m × 0.6 m** (depth along beam only 0.6 m), replacing the upstream photon-tagger. The physics goal is kinematically complete CC events with both muon and leading proton reconstructed, enabling transverse kinematic imbalance (TKI) analysis. Key challenges:

- ~25% of muons exit at >50° → need large-angle muon tracking
- ~35% of leading protons exit at >50° → need large-angle proton reconstruction
- Median proton momentum ~450 MeV/c → protons have short ranges (~10 cm in plastic), so spatial resolution and low-threshold tracking are critical
- 6% of protons exceed 900 MeV/c → dynamic range must be adequate
- Hydrocarbon target is acceptable
- Must reduce systematic uncertainty from ~6% to ~4%

---

## Proposed Upgrades

### 1. High-Granularity Plastic Scintillator Active Target (Primary Recommendation)

**Replace the photon-tagger volume with a fully-active scintillator cube detector** ("SuperCube" concept), filling most of the 2.0 × 1.9 × 0.6 m envelope.

**Design:**
- ~2 cm × 2 cm × 2 cm polystyrene scintillator cubes assembled into a 3D array, approximately 100 × 95 × 30 cubes ≈ 285,000 cubes
- Each cube read out on **three orthogonal faces** by wavelength-shifting (WLS) fibres routed to SiPMs, giving full 3D hit reconstruction by coincidence
- This is a proven concept (SuperFGD for T2K ND280 upgrade), directly applicable here
- Total polystyrene mass in this volume: ~2.0 × 1.9 × 0.6 m at ~1.05 g/cm³ × packing fraction ≈ **~2.3 t** of active hydrocarbon target

**Physics justification:**
- 2 cm cube size gives ~1 cm effective resolution, sufficient to reconstruct proton tracks down to ~300 MeV/c (range ~3–4 cubes) and stopping muons
- 4π-like solid-angle sensitivity — protons and muons escaping at large angles (>50°) are tracked within the cube volume or handed off to surrounding detectors before exiting
- Protons at 450 MeV/c have a range of ~11 cm in polystyrene → ~5–6 cubes, well-measured
- Protons up to ~900 MeV/c have range ~50–55 cm → can be fully contained within or near the 60 cm depth, depending on angle; for forward-going high-momentum protons that exit, they enter the downstream TPCs
- The granularity breaks the degeneracy between short proton tracks and nuclear fragments, critical for TKI
- SiPM readout gives good dE/dx PID to separate protons from pions

**Engineering:**
- WLS fibre + SiPM readout is the same technology already used in the existing detector's scintillator channels → common infrastructure, spares, and expertise
- Fibre routing in three axes requires careful mechanical assembly but is established (T2K SuperFGD production)
- Total SiPM channel count ~855,000 (three fibres per cube × 285,000 cubes); manageable with 64-channel CITIROC or similar ASICs at ~$0.10–0.20/channel at this scale
- Fits within existing magnet volume; existing downstream TPCs and tracking targets remain untouched

---

### 2. Thin-Wall Surrounding Mini-TPC or Straw-Tracker Shells (Secondary)

For muons and high-momentum protons that escape the cube volume laterally (the ~25–35% at >50°), add **two thin straw-tube tracker planes** (or small resistive-plate chambers) on the ±x and ±y faces of the cube assembly, each ~2 mm pitch, to extend tracking into the surrounding gas volume before particles reach the return-yoke scintillator.

- Straws can operate at atmospheric pressure in Ar:CO₂, low mass, low threshold
- Provides lever arm for momentum measurement by curvature in the 0.2 T dipole field for side-going tracks
- Bridges reconstruction between the cube and the existing yoke scintillator "ranger"

---

### 3. Timing Upgrade for SiPMs Throughout

Replace or supplement existing SiPM readout electronics with **fast-timing front-end boards** providing ~1 ns or better time resolution per channel.

- Time-of-flight between cube hits distinguishes protons (slow) from pions (fast) at momenta where dE/dx is ambiguous (~600–900 MeV/c)
- Improves vertex finding in the cube by rejecting out-of-time activity (e.g., neutron-induced secondaries)
- Sub-nanosecond SiPMs are commercially available; existing WLS fibre timing (~2–3 ns) is the limiting factor — transition to shorter-decay-time fluor (e.g., Y-11 → K-27 or EJ-280) increases photon arrival time resolution

---

### 4. Thin Gadolinium-Doped Water Layer Interleaving (Tertiary, Optional)

If water comparison within the new target is desired (beyond the existing downstream water-layer target), interleave **4–5 thin (1 cm) gadolinium-loaded water bags** within the cube assembly at intervals of ~6 cube layers.

- Gd captures neutrons with ~25 μs delayed gamma cascade → neutron tagging to constrain multinucleon (2p2h) backgrounds
- Keeps primary target hydrocarbon (C:H ratio dominated by polystyrene)
- Adds ~15 kg of water, negligible perturbation to tracking performance
- Improves modelling of nuclear effects relevant to the water far detector

---

### 5. Improved Downstream Interface: Thin Silicon Pixel Layer

Place a single layer of **thin silicon pixel sensors** (e.g., ALPIDE Monolithic Active Pixel Sensors, 50 μm thick) at the downstream face of the new active target.

- Provides a precise (~25 μm) reference hit for tracks entering the first downstream TPC
- Resolves track-matching ambiguity when multiple secondaries exit simultaneously
- ALPIDE is radiation-tolerant, low-power, and has been used in ALICE ITS — commercially available and well-understood
- One layer, 2.0 m × 1.9 m active area, requires ~400 chips at ~$50–100/chip → modest cost relative to other systems

---

## Summary Table

| Upgrade | Primary Benefit | Technical Readiness |
|---|---|---|
| 3D scintillator cube active target | Full proton + muon reconstruction, low threshold | High (T2K SuperFGD precedent) |
| Straw-tube lateral tracker shells | Large-angle track extension, momentum by curvature | High |
| Fast-timing SiPM electronics | ToF PID for proton/pion separation | High |
| Gd-water interleaving | Neutron tagging, 2p2h constraint | Medium |
| Silicon pixel downstream interface | Precise track handoff to TPCs | High |

---

## Expected Systematic Improvement

The 3D cube target eliminates the dominant contributions to the ~6% residual systematic:
- **Flux uncertainty** is constrained by the improved muon-neutrino CC sample statistics and kinematic coverage (TKI distributions are flux-shape sensitive)
- **Cross-section modelling** (FSI, 2p2h) is constrained by the complete proton reconstruction — currently the largest single contribution to residual systematics at ~3–4%
- With full proton reconstruction enabling TKI, the expected reduction is toward the **~3–3.5% level**, meeting the 4% goal

---

**TOP RECOMMENDATION:** Replace the upstream photon-tagger section with a fully-active 3D polystyrene scintillator cube detector (~2 cm × 2 cm × 2 cm cubes, three-axis WLS-fibre/SiPM readout) filling the available 2.0 m × 1.9 m × 0.6 m envelope, providing low-threshold large-angle proton and muon reconstruction needed for transverse kinematic imbalance analysis.

# Design Review Recommendations: ND280 Upstream Active Target

## Preamble: Physics-Driven Constraints

Before recommending hardware, I'll anchor each choice to the specific performance requirements:

- **Angular acceptance**: 25% of muons and 35% of protons exit beyond 50°, so the active target must provide near-4π tracking, not just forward acceptance
- **Proton momentum range**: median ~450 MeV/c means protons have ranges of ~9 cm in plastic scintillator; 6% exceed 900 MeV/c (range ~40 cm). The detector must handle both short-range stopping tracks and occasional punch-through
- **Volume constraint**: 2.0 m × 1.9 m × 0.6 m — the 0.6 m depth is tight and penalizes long radiation lengths
- **Goal**: kinematically complete CC events for transverse kinematic imbalance (TKI), requiring simultaneous muon-plus-proton reconstruction, reducing systematics from ~6% to ~4%

---

## Recommended Hardware Changes

### 1. Scintillator Cube Active Target ("SuperFGD-style") — PRIMARY TARGET VOLUME

**Technology**: A three-dimensional array of 1 cm × 1 cm × 1 cm optically-isolated polystyrene scintillator cubes, each read out by three orthogonal wavelength-shifting (WLS) fibres (one per axis), with silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs, specifically MPPCs — Multi-Pixel Photon Counters, as already qualified in ND280) on each fibre end.

**Specific implementation**: Approximately 192 × 184 × 56 cubes (~2.0 M channels for a fully-instrumented volume of ~192 × 184 × 56 cm), consistent with the available box. This matches the SuperFGD design already adopted by the T2K upgrade collaboration, which I am endorsing here on specific technical grounds rather than simply deferring to the choice.

**Justification**:

- *3D segmentation solves the large-angle problem*: Unlike the existing FGDs, which have planar x/y layers perpendicular to the beam and consequently degrade badly for tracks beyond ~45°, the cube geometry provides identical spatial resolution in all three projections regardless of track direction. A 50°-to-beam proton traverses roughly 1.5–2 cm of cubes before exiting any given face; with 1 cm pitch this gives 2–3 hits per plane regardless of azimuthal angle, preserving pattern recognition for the 35% of protons in the problematic angular regime
- *Proton range matching*: A 450 MeV/c proton (kinetic energy ~100 MeV) has a range of ~8–9 cm in polystyrene (density ~1.06 g/cm³). This is 8–9 cube lengths — enough for Bragg-peak identification and momentum-by-range measurement. A 900 MeV/c proton (~340 MeV kinetic energy) ranges out in ~35–40 cm, which fits comfortably within the 56 cm depth. This means the great majority of leading protons are *contained* and can be measured by range, which is more precise than curvature for these momenta given the modest 0.2 T field
- *Hydrocarbon target compatibility*: Polystyrene (C₈H₈) provides the hydrocarbon target explicitly stated as acceptable, with ~7% higher hydrogen fraction by mass than the existing FGD bars, marginally improving H-extraction statistics
- *Low cross-talk and high efficiency*: The optical isolation between cubes (achieved via surface treatment or thin reflective coating) ensures that charge disambiguation in 3D is robust. Each cube is effectively a 3D coincidence element: a true hit requires correlated signals on all three fibres, reducing noise hits
- *SiPM readout continuity*: MPPCs are already the ND280 standard (all ECal and FGD channels use them). The same MPPC model (Hamamatsu S13360-1325PE or equivalent 1.3 mm pitch, ~667 pixels/mm² to handle the light yield from 1 cm cubes) can be used, minimising new qualification effort. Existing slow-control, bias distribution, and DAQ firmware are reusable with modest modification

**Known risk**: The channel count (~2M fibres × 2 ends = ~4M SiPM channels before multiplexing) is large. This is mitigated by fibre multiplexing along each axis — the standard approach is to read groups of fibres with a single SiPM using a coded pattern so that only one cube is unambiguously lit per track crossing; with track multiplicities typical of these neutrino interactions (rarely more than 3–4 charged secondaries) ghost-hit rates are manageable. The collaboration should commission dedicated pattern-recognition simulations for the ND280 beam spectrum before finalising the multiplexing factor.

---

### 2. Time-of-Flight Panels Surrounding the Active Target

**Technology**: Thin (5–10 mm) plastic scintillator panels with SiPM readout on all six faces of the SuperFGD volume, targeting ≤200 ps timing resolution per panel.

**Justification**:

- *Proton–pion separation*: The critical background to kinematically complete CC-0π events is CC-1π where the pion is absorbed or misidentified. A 450 MeV/c proton and a 450 MeV/c π⁺ are both above Cherenkov threshold in scintillator, so dE/dx alone is marginal for separation in the cube volume. ToF between the interaction vertex (timestamped to ~1 ns by the cube hit cluster) and the exiting face panel at ~200 ps resolution gives β resolution sufficient to separate protons from pions up to ~600–700 MeV/c, covering the bulk of the momentum distribution
- *Direction disambiguation for large-angle tracks*: For tracks crossing multiple cube faces, ToF gives an unambiguous directionality that removes the left-right ambiguity that planar detectors suffer from at large angles
- *Neutron tagging (bonus)*: Neutron-induced recoils in the cubes produce delayed hits. The surrounding ToF panels can veto or tag these at the ~10 ns level, improving the CC-0n event selection used in some TKI analyses
- *Technology*: EJ-200 or BC-408 fast plastic scintillator, 5 mm thick, in tiles of ~20 × 20 cm² read by 6 mm × 6 mm SiPMs (e.g. SensL J-series or Hamamatsu S13360-6050). This is a mature technology with demonstrated performance in similar near-detector applications (e.g. NINJA, WAGASCI)

---

### 3. Upgrade of the Three TPCs to High-Pressure Operation or Replace the First TPC with a Resistive Micromegas TPC

**Technology**: For the immediately downstream TPC (TPC1, the first the muon encounters after the new target), replace or supplement the existing bulk Micromegas with **resistive Micromegas** using a resistive anode layer.

**Justification**:

- *Space-charge and rate handling*: The existing bulk Micromegas are susceptible to discharge damage and gain instability under the increased event rates expected in T2K-II (beam intensity increases by ~3×). Resistive Micromegas quench discharges passively without gain loss, extending detector lifetime without module replacement
- *Improved dE/dx resolution*: Resistive anodes reduce the capacitive cross-talk between adjacent pads, improving the cluster charge resolution by ~15–20% in comparable systems (NA61/SHINE, ALICE TPC upgrade). This directly improves proton–pion dE/dx separation in the TPC for tracks that escape the new target — specifically benefiting the 6% of protons above 900 MeV/c that are unlikely to range out in the SuperFGD
- *Muon momentum measurement*: For the 25% of muons exiting beyond 50°, some will re-enter the TPC gas volume at large angles. The existing readout pad geometry (rectangular pads oriented for near-forward tracks) can be supplemented with a rotated or diamond pad layout in a module dedicated to the upstream position, improving transverse-to-beam momentum resolution
- *Gas composition*: No change to Ar:CF₄:iC₄H₁₀ 95:3:2 is recommended — this mixture is well-characterised and the drift velocity and diffusion coefficients are known. Avoid the temptation to switch to a pure-Ar or Ar-CO₂ mixture for cost saving, as the existing calibration database would be invalidated

---

### 4. Thin Upstream Veto / Gamma Catcher Panel

**Technology**: Two planes of 3 cm × 3 cm cross-section triangular scintillator bars (identical to P0D bars, already tooled) in x and y, placed immediately upstream of the SuperFGD, read by WLS fibre and MPPC.

**Justification**:

- *Beam-related background rejection*: Charged particles entering the new target from upstream (halo muons, beam-related backgrounds from the upstream beamline) must be vetoed to avoid contaminating the neutrino interaction sample. Two planes of triangular bars in x and y provide >98% geometric coverage with the interlocking cross-section design, which is already proven in the P0D
- *Cost and schedule*: Since the P0D is being removed, its scintillator bars, WLS fibres, and MPPC mounting hardware are available for reuse. This reduces the cost of the veto to essentially the light-tight enclosure and new front-end electronics, and leverages the collaboration's existing experience with this technology
- *Minimal radiation length*: At ~2 cm total polystyrene equivalent upstream of the target, the material budget is ~0.023 X₀, negligible for the muon and proton tracking goals

---

### 5. DAQ and Trigger: Self-Triggering Readout ASIC for the SuperFGD

**Technology**: Deploy the **CITIROC** (Cherenkov Imaging Telescope with Integrating ReadOut Chip) or the successor **PETIROC** ASIC, or the ATLAS-heritage **VMM3a** ASIC, for SiPM signal processing, with a triggerless (self-triggering) architecture feeding a software-based event builder.

**Justification**:

- *Channel density*: The ~4M SiPM channels of the SuperFGD (after multiplexing down to ~50,000–100,000 electronic channels) cannot be read by the existing ND280 Trip-t-based FGD electronics without significant re-engineering. The VMM3a integrates shaping, discriminator, peak-hold ADC, and time-to-digital converter in a single chip handling 64 channels, with proven performance in the NSW upgrade of ATLAS. Its dynamic range (4 fC to ~10 pC) covers the SiPM signal range from a single photoelectron to a heavily-ionising proton Bragg peak
- *Triggerless operation*: The T2K beam spill is 8 bunches × ~58 ns width within a ~5 μs window. A triggerless readout that timestamps every hit above threshold and builds events offline is more robust to in-spill pile-up than a hardware-triggered system, and is consistent with the broader HEP trend toward continuous readout. This also facilitates neutron-capture tagging at the microsecond timescale for future analyses
- *Integration with existing systems*: The existing ND280 DAQ uses a COPPER/FINESSE-based system. The new SiPM front-ends should output data via standard GBT (Gigabit Transceiver) optical links compatible with the FELIX (Front-End LInk eXchange) PCIe readout card, which is now the LHC standard and for which ND280 should adopt compatible infrastructure during this upgrade to future-proof the system

---

## Summary Table

| Change | Technology | Key Benefit |
|---|---|---|
| 3D scintillator cube target | 1 cm³ PS cubes + 3-axis WLS fibre + MPPC | 4π tracking, proton containment |
| Surrounding ToF panels | Fast plastic scintillator + SiPM | p/π separation, directionality |
| Resistive Micromegas TPC1 upgrade | Resistive anode layer on existing geometry | Rate robustness, improved dE/dx |
| Upstream veto planes | Reused P0D triangular bars + MPPC | Background rejection, low cost |
| Self-triggering DAQ ASICs | VMM3a + GBT/FELIX | Channel density, pile-up handling |

---

## Critical Caveat for the Panel

The 0.6 m depth constraint is the single most important number in this review. The collaboration must run full GEANT4 simulations of proton ranging in the proposed cube geometry — specifically verifying that the containment fraction for leading protons is sufficient to meet the TKI systematic target — before committing to the transverse dimensions of the cube array, because there is a direct trade-off between the number of target-mass cubes (which determines statistics) and the buffer depth needed for proton containment (which determines the systematic on proton momentum).

---

TOP RECOMMENDATION: Replace the P0D volume with a 3D array of 1 cm³ optically-isolated polystyrene scintillator cubes read out by three orthogonal WLS fibres and MPPCs (SuperFGD architecture), because it simultaneously solves the large-angle acceptance problem for both muons and protons, provides proton momentum measurement by range for the bulk of the momentum spectrum, and uses already-qualified SiPM technology — directly enabling the kinematically complete CC event reconstruction required to reduce the near-detector systematic uncertainty from 6% to 4%.

# Design Review Recommendations for Kestrel Flats Near Detector Active Target

## Analysis of Requirements

The key constraints are:
1. **Geometric coverage**: 4π acceptance including backward-going tracks
2. **Low momentum threshold**: ~60 MeV kinetic energy protons (∼350 MeV/c momentum)
3. **Hydrogen constraint**: ≤2% of target nucleons
4. **Volume**: 2.6 m × 2.3 m × 0.9 m in 0.15 T field
5. **Neutrino energy**: ~0.7 GeV beam

## Recommended Hardware Configuration

### 1. **Time Projection Chamber with Micromegas Readout**

**Technology**: A high-pressure gaseous TPC with bulk Micromegas (MICRO-MEsh GAseous Structure) readout planes on all six faces.

**Justification**:
- **4π coverage**: TPC naturally provides full solid angle acceptance since tracks can be reconstructed in any direction, including backward
- **Low threshold**: Gas allows ~60 MeV protons to produce measurable ionization tracks (range ~2-3 cm in Ar at atmospheric pressure)
- **3D tracking**: Drift time + 2D pixel readout gives complete 3D reconstruction
- **Low hydrogen content**: Can use pure Ar or Ar/CO₂ mixtures (essentially zero hydrogen)
- **Proven technology**: Used successfully in T2K ND280 upgrade, ALICE, and proposed for DUNE

**Specific parameters**:
- Gas: Ar:CO₂ (90:10) or Ar:CF₄ (95:5) at atmospheric or slightly elevated pressure
- Drift field: ~400 V/cm (compatible with 0.15 T)
- Micromegas amplification gaps on all six walls
- Pixel pitch: 3-5 mm for adequate position resolution

### 2. **Target Planes Upstream: Solid CH₂ Interleaved with TPCs**

**Technology**: Thin (1-2 cm) polyethylene (CH₂) targets positioned immediately upstream of the main TPC volume, instrumented with thin scintillator planes for timing/trigger.

**Justification**:
- **Hydrogen access**: Provides pure hydrogen interactions needed for analysis
- **Low mass fraction**: Can keep hydrogen nucleon fraction ≤2% with thin targets
- **Vertex identification**: Scintillator timing identifies which plane had the interaction
- **Minimal perturbation**: Tracks exit into TPC for full reconstruction

**Configuration**:
- 3-4 planes of 1 cm CH₂ with 1 mm plastic scintillator + SiPM readout
- Total ~4 cm CH₂ in 90 cm depth = ~1.5% by nucleon count (accounting for TPC gas)

### 3. **Resistive Plate Chambers (RPCs) Surrounding TPC**

**Technology**: Thin glass RPCs outside the Micromegas planes on the four lateral faces and downstream face.

**Justification**:
- **Timing reference**: ~1 ns timing resolution for t₀ determination
- **Trigger**: Fast signal for neutrino interaction candidate identification
- **Through-going muon tagging**: Identifies muons exiting to downstream spectrometer
- **Low mass**: Glass RPCs add minimal material
- **Cost-effective**: Simpler and cheaper than additional trackers

**Specification**:
- 2 mm glass gap RPCs
- Strips or pads at 1-2 cm pitch
- Coverage on 5 faces (all except most upstream)

### 4. **Enhanced Field Cage Design**

**Technology**: Ultra-low mass field cage using thin Kapton-copper strips and ceramic standoffs.

**Justification**:
- **Minimize interactions outside fiducial volume**: Standard Al field cages create significant inactive material
- **Maintain drift uniformity**: Critical for position reconstruction
- **Transparency**: Low-Z materials preserve track energy measurement

### 5. **High-Granularity Pixel Readout Electronics**

**Technology**: Custom ASIC with per-pixel charge and timing measurement (e.g., T2K ND280 upgrade AFTER chip or similar).

**Justification**:
- **dE/dx measurement**: Particle identification of protons vs. pions
- **Multiple tracks**: High-multiplicity event reconstruction at 0.7 GeV
- **Stopping proton ID**: Critical for low-energy threshold

**Specification**:
- ~500k channels total
- Charge resolution ~15%
- Timing resolution ~100 ns (binning drift time)

### 6. **Calibration Systems**

**Technology**: 
- UV laser system for electron drift monitoring
- Radioactive source deployment (Fe-55, Am-241)
- Cosmic ray trigger system

**Justification**:
- **Drift velocity monitoring**: Critical for position accuracy
- **Gain calibration**: Essential for dE/dx and threshold stability
- **Spatial calibration**: Cosmic rays provide through-going tracks

## Alternative Considered and Rejected

**3D plastic scintillator**: While providing good timing and 4π coverage, it has:
- Too much hydrogen (~14% by nucleon count in CH-based scintillator)
- Poor momentum resolution
- Difficulty reconstructing short proton tracks

**Silicon vertex detector + passive target**: 
- Excellent resolution but very expensive
- Power dissipation challenging in gas volume
- Still needs gas TPC for 4π coverage anyway

## Implementation Priority

The collaboration should implement these in order:
1. TPC with Micromegas (core functionality)
2. Pixel readout electronics (enables full TPC performance)
3. RPC trigger/timing system (enables operation)
4. CH₂ target planes (enables hydrogen measurements)
5. Calibration systems (enables physics quality data)
6. Field cage optimization (performance enhancement)

**TOP RECOMMENDATION: High-pressure gaseous TPC with 6-plane Micromegas readout providing complete 4π coverage and low-threshold tracking**

# Proposed ND280-style upgrade for the vacated photon-tagging volume

## Why the current detector falls short

The existing tracker is built for forward-going tracks:

- **Bar orientation:** the target bars are all perpendicular to the beam, and the TPCs sit only downstream. High-angle and backward muons and protons cross few bars, or no TPC at all.
- **Missing kinematics:** about 25% of muons and 35% of leading protons exit at more than 50°. That is a large, model-dependent hole in acceptance, and it makes the transverse kinematic imbalance (TKI) final state incomplete.
- **Proton thresholds:** a 1 cm bar in a two-view x/y geometry has poor efficiency for short proton tracks. The median proton (450 MeV/c, T ≈ 100 MeV) ranges only about 8–10 cm in CH.

The upgrade therefore needs three things:
1. A fully active, finely segmented, three-dimensional (isotropic) target.
2. Gas tracking that covers high angles.
3. Precise timing on all faces.

## 1. Fine-grained 3D scintillator-cube target ("SuperFGD")

This fills the ~2.0 × 1.9 × 0.6 m box.

**Geometry**
- About 192 × 182 × 56 ≈ 2 million optically isolated 1 × 1 × 1 cm³ polystyrene cubes.
- The scintillator is doped with PTP/POPOP and given an etched reflective (chemical) surface coating.
- Total mass is about 2 t of CH, roughly doubling the existing target mass.

**Readout**
- Each cube has three orthogonal 1.5 mm holes carrying 1 mm Y-11 multiclad wavelength-shifting fibres along x, y and z.
- That gives three 2D projections and true 3D matching, with about 56,000 channels.
- Fibres are read out at one end by 1.3 mm-pixel MPPCs (Hamamatsu S13360-class); the far ends are mirrored.
- Electronics are CITIROC-based front-end boards, giving about 1 ns time resolution per channel and ~0.5–0.9 ns per cube when combined.

**What it delivers**
- **Isotropic acceptance:** muons and protons are reconstructed out to 90° and backward.
- **Low proton threshold:** protons are tracked from about 300 MeV/c (2–3 cubes) upward.
- **Proton momentum by range** up to roughly 700–800 MeV/c, with dE/dx in each cube for p/π/μ separation.
- **Neutrons:** secondary scatters can be identified and their energy measured by time of flight inside the cube volume, adding the neutron to TKI on antineutrino CC0π events.
- **Photon/π⁰ detection:** this partly recovers the lost photon-tagging function. Electron–gamma separation can use the vertex gap and dE/dx.

## 2. Two high-angle TPCs above and below the new target

These sit where the old section's top and bottom clearances allow, inside the magnet.

**Construction**
- Each is about 2.0 × 0.8 × 1.8 m (drift along x), with the same argon-based gas mixture as the existing TPCs (Ar:CF₄:iC₄H₁₀ 95:3:2).
- The field cage is a thin composite laminate (aramid honeycomb, Kevlar/fibreglass, copper strips), about 4% X₀, to limit multiple scattering and photon conversions.

**Readout**
- Resistive bulk Micromegas with an encapsulated resistive anode (ERAM), about 1 × 1 cm pads, 16 modules per endplate.
- Charge spreading gives better than 600 µm spatial resolution and dE/dx resolution below 10%.
- AFTER/AGET-based front ends.

**Purpose**
- Momentum measurement by curvature in the 0.2 T field for high-angle muons and the ~6% of protons above 900 MeV/c that exit the cube target.
- Charge-sign and PID matching to the existing downstream TPCs and calorimeters.

## 3. Time-of-flight envelope

**Construction**
- Six panels enclose the new target and the high-angle TPCs.
- Each panel uses 2.2 m long, ~12 cm wide, 1 cm thick EJ-200 cast plastic bars.
- Arrays of 6 × 6 mm² SiPMs couple to both ends of each bar, read out with waveform digitisers (SAMPIC-class).
- Time resolution is about 150 ps per bar.

**Purpose**
- **Track direction:** distinguishes inward from outward-going tracks, rejecting out-of-fiducial-volume and sand-muon backgrounds that mimic backward tracks.
- **Particle ID:** adds β-based identification, for example separating protons from π⁺ around 1 GeV/c.
- **Shared timing reference:** provides the common start time for neutron time of flight in the cube target.

## 4. Supporting changes

- **Triggering and data acquisition:** upgrade to accommodate ~70,000 new SiPM channels and the high-angle TPC pads, with a common clock synchronised to the beam spill.
- **Calorimeter and side-muon coverage:** extend the yoke-gap scintillator and lead-scintillator calorimeter coverage around the new volume where the old section's calorimeter is removed.
- **Calibration:** in-situ LED/laser calibration of the SiPMs, plus cosmic-ray calibration of cube light yield (~50 p.e. per fibre per minimum-ionising particle) and of cube-to-cube optical crosstalk (~3%).
- **Carbon-to-water comparison:** keep the downstream water-layer target, and use matched event selections between the CH-cube sample and the water sample.

## Expected impact

Together these give near-4π reconstruction of the muon and leading proton in charged-current events. This enables TKI variables (δp_T, δα_T, δφ_T) and neutron-tagged antineutrino samples.

Greater acceptance plus the doubled target mass target the roughly 2-percentage-point reduction needed in flux and cross-section systematics, from ~6% to ~4%.

TOP RECOMMENDATION: Replace the photon-tagging section with a ~2-tonne fully active 3D-readout target of 1 cm³ scintillator cubes ("SuperFGD", three orthogonal WLS fibres per cube read by SiPMs), complemented by high-angle resistive-Micromegas TPCs and a ToF envelope.

Based on the detector description and physics requirements, here are my proposed hardware upgrades:

## 1. **SuperFGD-style 3D Scintillator Cube Target**

**Technology:** Fine-grained 3D segmented plastic scintillator with three orthogonal wavelength-shifting fiber readouts per cube (1 cm³ voxels), filling the ~2.0 × 1.9 × 0.6 m upstream space.

**Physics motivation:** The current 2D alternating x/y bar configuration cannot efficiently reconstruct particles at >50° to the beam. True 3D readout enables full angular acceptance for the ~25% of muons and ~35% of protons emerging at large angles. Three-view matching provides redundancy for track reconstruction and improved particle identification. The fine 1 cm granularity allows proton tracking down to ~300 MeV/c kinetic energy while maintaining angular resolution needed for transverse kinematic imbalance measurements.

## 2. **Time-of-Flight System**

**Technology:** Thin (1-2 cm) fast plastic scintillator planes with SiPM readout at both the upstream entrance and downstream exit of the new target volume, with ~100 ps timing resolution.

**Physics motivation:** Discriminates protons from pions in the critical 300-700 MeV/c momentum range where range-based PID becomes ambiguous. Essential for correctly identifying the "leading proton" and reducing systematic uncertainties from pion misidentification in CCQE-like event selection. The 60 cm flight path provides ~500 ps separation between protons and pions at 450 MeV/c.

## 3. **Enhanced Gas TPC Field Configuration**

**Technology:** Modify the three TPCs to run at higher drift field (400 V/cm vs typical 200 V/cm) with upgraded readout electronics for improved dE/dx resolution.

**Physics motivation:** Better particle identification for protons exiting the target, particularly in the 450-900 MeV/c range where dE/dx discrimination between protons and minimum-ionizing particles is crucial. Improves containment tagging and enables better momentum measurement for forward-going protons that penetrate into the TPCs.

## 4. **Side Scintillator Hodoscope Planes**

**Technology:** Additional thin scintillator tracking planes on the four lateral sides of the new target volume, instrumented with strips or bars for position measurement.

**Physics motivation:** Critical for catching the large-angle muons and protons (>50° to beam) that would otherwise escape laterally without adequate tracking. Provides timing and trajectory information to match backward-going or sideways-going tracks to the neutrino vertex, reducing backgrounds from rock muons and improving vertex resolution for transverse momentum balance studies.

## 5. **Hybrid Target with Water Layers**

**Technology:** Segment the 60 cm depth into 40 cm of 3D scintillator backed by 20 cm of water layers (2 cm thick) interleaved with thin scintillator tracking planes.

**Physics motivation:** Provides direct water-target events in the upstream detector for immediate comparison with the far detector target material, reducing reliance on the downstream water target for nuclear model systematics. The water fraction provides ~0.5 ton fiducial mass while maintaining tracking capability for particles exiting water interactions.

## 6. **Improved Magnetic Field Mapping**

**Technology:** Install Hall probe arrays and NMR measurement system for precision field mapping throughout the magnet volume, with continuous monitoring.

**Physics motivation:** Momentum scale uncertainties directly affect the transverse kinematic imbalance reconstruction. Reducing field uncertainty from ~2% to <0.5% is necessary to achieve the 4% systematic target, particularly for muons that curve in the magnetic field and low-momentum protons where multiple scattering becomes significant.

## 7. **Neutron Tagging Calorimetry**

**Technology:** Add boron-loaded plastic scintillator or gadolinium-doped layers to the downstream electromagnetic calorimeter, or install dedicated neutron capture detectors.

**Physics motivation:** Final-state neutrons carry away invisible energy, affecting the transverse momentum balance. Even partial neutron detection (via capture gammas at ~100 ns delays) allows statistical corrections to the kinematic reconstruction and enables studies of multinucleon effects, reducing model-dependent uncertainties in the flux and cross-section extraction.

---

**TOP RECOMMENDATION: SuperFGD-style 3D Scintillator Cube Target**

The 3D segmented scintillator target is the single most important upgrade because it directly addresses the fundamental limitation: current 2D readout cannot reconstruct the large-angle particles that dominate systematic uncertainties in transverse kinematic studies. Without true 3D tracking and the resulting full angular acceptance, the other upgrades cannot achieve their potential, and the 4% systematic goal remains out of reach.

# Proposed hardware upgrades for the Kestrel Flats near-detector target region

## 1. What the hydrogen limit rules out

The usual choice for a 4π active target is a finely segmented plastic-scintillator detector (SuperFGD-type). It does not fit here:

- In CH, hydrogen is about 1 nucleon in 13, roughly 7.7% of target nucleons.
- Water-based targets are worse, at about 11%.
- Both exceed the 2% limit at which the hydrogen-subtraction model stays valid.

The active target therefore has to be a hydrogen-free medium. Since the far detector contains no hydrogen, argon is the natural choice, and it also lets you match the far-detector nucleus if the far detector is argon. Argon contributes 0% hydrogen. Hydrogen would enter only through structural materials such as G10 and FR4, so keep these outside or at the edge of the fiducial volume.

## 2. Core upgrade: a modular liquid-argon TPC with pixel readout

Fill the 2.6 × 2.3 × 0.9 m region with a compact ArgonCube/ND-LAr–style modular LArTPC.

**Cryostat**
- Use a vacuum-insulated, low-mass cryostat that fits inside the warm dipole.
- Make the downstream window thin aluminium or a composite, to minimise scattering before the existing drift chambers.
- The warm magnet field is unaffected by the cryostat.

**Active volume**
- Expect roughly 2.3 × 2.0 × 0.75 m active, about 5 t of LAr.
- That gives roughly a 4 t fiducial mass.

**Drift geometry**
- Split the volume into several optically isolated modules with short drift lengths, about 30–50 cm, and a transverse drift direction.
- Short drifts keep the cathode HV modest, at roughly 25–50 kV.
- They also limit diffusion and reduce the sensitivity to argon purity and space charge.
- The ~2% hydrogen limit applies to the target nucleons, so plan the module structure accordingly.

**Charge readout**
- Use a pixelated anode (LArPix-type ASICs, ~4 mm pixels) rather than wire planes.
- This gives true 3D readout without wire ambiguities, which matters for event-to-event pileup at a near site.
- Pixel PCBs (FR4) sit at the module boundaries, outside the fiducial region.

**Light readout**
- Fit fast scintillation-light detectors (ArCLight or light-collection modules with SiPMs) on the field-cage walls of each module.
- They should give ns-level timing.
- This assigns each interaction to its beam bunch and to the drift t₀.
- It also separates beam-correlated "rock" muons and neutrons from in-target events.

**How this meets the physics requirements**

*Protons:*
- A 60 MeV proton has a range of only about 3 cm in LAr.
- With ~4 mm pixels this is a resolvable track of roughly 8 hits, with calorimetric dE/dx for particle ID.
- The threshold is effectively lower than 60 MeV, and isotropic, because no tracking planes are oriented along a preferred direction.

*Muons at all angles:*
- The LArTPC images tracks equally well forward, perpendicular and backward.
- This removes the angular acceptance hole that plane trackers have.

## 3. Muon momentum and charge for tracks that miss the downstream chambers

Forward muons exit into the existing downstream drift chambers, which measure momentum and charge in the 0.15 T field. High-angle and backward muons do not reach them. Several measures cover those tracks.

**Momentum by range or scattering**
- Use range for muons stopping in the LAr. Below about 300 MeV/c they stop within a metre.
- Use multiple-Coulomb-scattering fitting for exiting muons. This typically gives 10–20% resolution with a LArTPC.

**Side and upstream trackers in the magnet gap**
- Line the gap between the cryostat and the magnet yoke with thin gas trackers (Micromegas or resistive-anode TPC modules, or thin drift chambers) on the top, bottom, left, right and upstream faces.
- They measure the curvature of side- and backward-exiting muons in the 0.15 T field. This provides charge, which is needed for sign selection, and adds a momentum lever arm.
- These trackers are outside the target volume, so their hydrogen content does not count against the 2% limit.

**Time-of-flight envelope**
- Add a fast scintillator time-of-flight layer (~150 ps) around the cryostat and trackers.
- It resolves forward versus backward direction for exiting tracks, so backward-going muons are not mistaken for incoming ones.
- It also tags incoming particles as a veto.

**Muon tagging outside the magnet**
- Instrument the dipole return yoke with scintillator planes, as in an SMRD.
- This tags and ranges high-angle muons that penetrate the yoke.

Together these give well above 25% muon efficiency in every angular bin. Check this with a dedicated simulation.

## 4. Supporting systems

**Cryogenics**
- Argon purification for an electron lifetime above 1 ms.
- Recirculation and a cryocooler or LN₂ condenser.
- Oxygen-deficiency and safety systems appropriate to an underground or near-surface hall.

**Calibration**
- UV laser tracks to map drift distortions and field non-uniformity from the magnet and cryostat.
- Cosmic and through-going muons for dE/dx scale.
- A pulsed charge-injection system for the pixel ASICs.

**Data acquisition**
- A triggerless pixel readout synchronised to the beam spill clock.
- Light-system timing to tag each bunch.

## 5. Option for very low thresholds

A high-pressure gaseous argon TPC (about 10 bar, ND-GAr style) could form a small sub-volume. It offers few-MeV proton thresholds and native magnetic momentum and charge measurement, also with no hydrogen.

Its main drawback is mass: the whole region would hold only about 0.1 t, giving poor statistics. It is therefore better as a complementary sample than as the main target.

TOP RECOMMENDATION: Replace the target region with a hydrogen-free modular liquid-argon TPC using pixelated 3D charge readout and fast SiPM light detection, surrounded by thin gas trackers and TOF in the magnet gap.

# Hardware Upgrade Proposals for the ND280 Upstream Active Target

## Core Design Concept: SuperFGD-Style Fully-Active 3D Scintillator Cube Target

The box available (~2.0 m × 1.9 m × 0.6 m) naturally motivates a segmented 3D target that provides both the active neutrino interaction medium and tracking capability with 4π acceptance for large-angle tracks.

---

## 1. Primary Target: 3D Segmented Scintillator Cube Array (SuperFGD)

**Technology:** ~1 cm × 1 cm × 1 cm extruded polystyrene scintillator cubes, each with three orthogonal holes through which wavelength-shifting (WLS) fibres (Kuraray Y-11, 1 mm diameter) pass in X, Y, and Z directions.

**Concrete specification:**
- Cube array approximately 192 × 182 × 56 cubes (X×Y×Z) filling the available volume
- ~1.96 million cubes total, mass ~1.9 t
- Each fibre read out by a Hamamatsu S13360-1325PE MPPC (1.3 mm × 1.3 mm, 25 μm pixel pitch, ~667 pixels) at the fibre ends
- Total MPPC channels: ~(192+182+56) × (corresponding transverse planes) → roughly 56,000–70,000 channels
- Cubes are assembled by threading fibres through pre-extruded holes and held in a carbon-fibre or aluminium frame; no gluing required between cubes (the fibres provide mechanical cohesion)

**Why this is critical:**
- The 3D topology gives genuine 4π tracking; for protons at >50° (35% of events per the specification), a conventional layered FGD-style detector loses them, but here the same cube is simultaneously read in three projections
- For the median proton momentum of ~450 MeV/c (range ~15 cm in polystyrene), a 1 cm voxel gives ~15 cubes of track, fully contained and reconstructed
- Protons up to ~900 MeV/c (range ~50 cm) can still be tracked and range-measured within the volume

---

## 2. High-Angle Muon Tracker: Thin-Gap Time Projection Chambers (HA-TPCs)

**Technology:** Two resistive Micromegas or bulk-Micromegas TPCs placed on the lateral faces (top/bottom and left/right) of the cube target, inside the magnet volume.

**Concrete specification:**
- Active area per TPC: ~1.8 m × 0.5 m
- Drift gas: Ar:CF4:iC4H10 95:3:2 (same as existing TPCs, minimizing infrastructure changes)
- Drift distance: 25 cm maximum (keeps ion drift time manageable)
- Pad size: 1.0 cm × 0.7 cm resistive bulk Micromegas (same technology as existing ND280 TPCs, with resistive layer 100 kΩ/□ to suppress sparking)
- 4 TPCs total (two lateral pairs), each with ~1,300 pads
- Readout: AFTER ASIC (existing T2K choice) or upgrade to DREAM/AFTER ASIC at 50 MHz sampling, 511 time bins

**Why this matters:**
- 25% of muons exit at >50° and would miss the downstream TPC1; the lateral HA-TPCs capture these tracks and provide momentum measurement via curvature in the 0.2 T field
- The existing downstream TPC chain still handles forward muons
- The existing magnet field is already well-characterized, so no new field-mapping campaign is needed

---

## 3. Time-of-Flight (TOF) System Around the Cube Target

**Technology:** Plastic scintillator slabs (Eljen EJ-200 or equivalent) with SiPM readout on both ends.

**Concrete specification:**
- Slab dimensions: 2.0 m × 0.2 m × 0.5 cm (thickness), arranged as six planar layers (top, bottom, left, right, upstream face, downstream face)
- SiPMs: Hamamatsu S13360-6025PE (6 mm × 6 mm, 25 μm pitch) at each end, two per slab
- Expected time resolution: σ_t ~ 200–250 ps (single slab), achieved with existing scintillator+SiPM technology
- ~120 slabs, ~240 SiPM channels total
- Triggered by coincidence logic in existing ND280 DAQ

**Why this matters:**
- TOF at 200 ps resolution over a 60 cm path length (~2 ns flight time for 450 MeV/c proton vs. pion) gives proton/pion separation up to ~1.1 GeV/c, which covers >94% of the leading proton spectrum (since only 6% exceed 900 MeV/c)
- Pion contamination in the leading "proton" sample is a major systematic for transverse kinematic imbalance (TKI); clean p/π separation directly reduces the ~6% residual systematic
- TOF also provides an independent vertex timing tag at ~250 ps, suppressing out-of-time pile-up from beam bunches

## 4. Downstream Transition Radiation Tracker or Extended ECAL Coverage

**Technology:** Extend the Pb-scintillator electromagnetic calorimeter coverage to wrap around the new target on the upstream face.

**Concrete specification:**
- Add one upstream ECAL module: Pb absorber plates (1.75 mm per layer, ~11 radiation lengths total), interspersed with scintillator bars (1 cm × 4 cm × 190 cm, Kuraray SCSF-38 WLS, MPPC readout)
- 50 layers, 11 X₀, ~400 kg
- Fits within the upstream face of the available box

**Why this matters:**
- π⁰ from neutral-current background and from CC resonance production must be vetoed; the existing ECAL coverage has a gap at the upstream face of the new target

**Concrete specification:**

- White Rabbit Ethernet nodes (CERN WR-ZEN) on each FEB for sub-nanosecond synchronization between TOF, TPC, and cube target, referenced to the J-PARC RF
